q-44192.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14189205/assets/dbf33e6d3a9e1efb4d0217f9076b0eb1381ea7d7fa9efa7ef7759b1c0e20175c.png)

The line shown above passes through the points $(0,3)$ and $(2,0).$ What is the equation of the line?
q-44192.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

From the graph, we see that the line intercepts the $y$-axis at $(0,3).$ So, the $y$-intercept is $b=3.$

We can calculate the slope of the line by choosing two points on the line and applying the slope formula. The line passes through the points $(0,3)$ and $(2,0),$ so we calculate its slope as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{0-3}{2-0} \\  & =\frac{-3}{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the slope $m=-\frac{3}{2}$ and the $y$-intercept $b=3$ into the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b,$ we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
y=-\frac{3}{2}x+3
$$

q-44192.html:
Question 1
?

The line shown above passes through the points (0,3) and (2,0). What is the equation of the line?

a
y=−32x
b
y=−3x+3
c
y=−32x+3
d
y=−3x+32
e
y=−x+3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form y=mx+b. So we need to work out the slope m and the y-intercept b.

From the graph, we see that the line intercepts the y-axis at (0,3). So, the y-intercept is b=3.

We can calculate the slope of the line by choosing two points on the line and applying the slope formula. The line passes through the points (0,3) and (2,0), so we calculate its slope as follows: m=y2−y1x2−x1=0−32−0=−32=−32

Substituting the slope m=−32 and the y-intercept b=3 into the slope-intercept form y=mx+b, we obtain the equation of the line:

y=−32x+3

q-178577.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14189205/assets/051c906be77d7e12a778449883a630c3b24f92b84ae7dac3d93b1787824f9c0c.png)

Consider the line shown above, which has a slope of $\frac{2}{3}.$ The equation of the line is $y=${{field-1}}.
q-178577.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ We know that the slope is $m=\frac{2}{3},$ so we just need to work out $y$-intercept $b.$

From the graph, we see that the line passes through the point $(3,3).$ Substituting this into $y=mx+b$ with $m=\frac{2}{3}$ and solving for $b,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{2}{3}x+b \\ 3 & =\frac{2}{3}(3)+b \\ 3 & =2+b \\ b & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is $y=\frac{2}{3}x+1.$

q-179508.name: Question 3
q-179508.problem:
Written in the form $y=mx+b,$ what is the equation of the line that passes through the points $(6,-2)$ and $(0,2)?$

The equation of the line is $y=$
{{field-1}}.
q-179508.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So, we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

First, we calculate the slope $m$ using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{2-(-2)}{0-6} \\  & =\frac{2+2}{0-6} \\  & =\frac{4}{-6} \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The coordinates of the $y$-intercept are always $(0,b).$ We know that the line passes through the point $(0,2),$ so the $y$-intercept is $b=2.$  

Substituting the slope $m=-\frac{2}{3}$ and the $y$-intercept $b=2$ into the slope-intercept formula $y=mx+b,$ we reach

$$
y=-\frac{2}{3}x+2.
$$
